mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discounting of expected corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% and remains >1% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: tightening cycle in the Fed funds rate
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified tightening window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening labor market strength and supply-side pressures, predicting negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO decreases over the same month
regime_hint: labor market weakening with supply contraction
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar labor market weakening events (backtest).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) above 5% for three months indicates resilient consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly average > 5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during qualifying demand periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the Industrial Production index (INDPRO) below 90 (monthly) coinciding with a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL < 225) suggests supply-side softness, predicting negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 90 and CPIAUCSL < 225 in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative in >80% of similar supply shocks (walk-forward).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in unemployment (UNRATE < 4.5%) over two consecutive months indicate a strong labor market, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns during an expansionary bias.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive during the identified labor expansion (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 150,000 in a month followed by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL < 230) suggests a strong labor market offset by deflationary pressures, predicting negative S&P 500 60-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 150,000 and CPIAUCSL < 230 in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not negative in >60% of similar events (backtest).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the 3-month moving average of industrial production (GDPC1 < 12000) reflects weak manufacturing momentum, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative during such periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand proxy (HOUST) suggest systemic supply constraints, predicting negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous and HOUST < previous in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative in >70% of such dual declines (walk-forward).
